sentences.text: The recording is about to begin.
Turn to page 3 of the Data File you have chosen.
OK, everyone, now we come to item three on the agenda, the campus food and drink.
I think we have a lot to discuss here.
Donnie, would you update us?
Yeah. As you might know, we've been having a few problems lately.
What kind of problems?
Well to start with there have been complaints about the food and the service in some of our cantines and restaurants.
Were these general complaints or something more specific about one incident?
Right, well, we received a complaint letter from a student, Gracie Ma.
You have a copy of the letter in your file.
I’ve since been in touch with her and got some more details.
She said that it happened on January the 3rd.
She became ill after eating a smoked salmon sandwich in the Coffee Shop.
She’s blaming the food in the Coffee Shop.
But people get ill for all sorts of reasons.
True, but the doctor at the university clinic said it was food poisoning.
Food poisoning? That’s serious.
So how do they think she got food poisoning?
Well, seemingly the likely cause is the smoked salmon she had in her sandwich.
You know, salmon can be a real problem.
I mean, if it’s not kept properly, it can easily go bad.
Yeah. So have you carried out any follow -up action?
Have you checked the Coffee Shop?
Yes, we carried out an inspection of the coffee Shop on Monday the 9th of January and You mean yesterday?
Yeah sorry, We carried out an inspection of the Coffee Shop yesterday, the 9th of January, and we found that the ingredients for the sandwiches, like the the smoked salmon,
the meat, tomatoes, lettuce, that kind of thing, were kept for long periods of time out of the fridge.
So, basically, as they’d been leaving all the food out of the fridge for so long, it wasn’t fresh and had gone off.
That’s awful, though I’m not surprised.
Yes, another thing was that there were insects.
Where? In the coffee shop?
Yes. We found evidence of cockroaches.
Ugh! Cockroaches! I won’t be eating there again.
I can tell you.
I know. Disgusting, isn’t it.
Yeah. Makes you think, doesn’t it.
Hmm. Was there anything else?
Yeah, the staff making the sandwiches didn't wear plastic disposable gloves I mean like they’re supposed to.
You know those plastic gloves you see people in sandwich places wearing when they’re preparing food?
Yeah. Well, they weren’t wearing them.
Well, we need to address all of these issues, obviously.
Any ideas about what can be done?
You’re right. We obviously need to do something.
Yeah, well, I’ve been in touch with the manager, Oliver Rogers about all of this, and I’ll be informing him of the results of our inspection and telling him that improvements need to be made.
And what else can we do if he doesn’t make these improvements?
If things don’t get better?
If these improvements aren’t made, I suggest we tell him we will not renew his contract.
Oliver Rogers, you mean?
Yeah. Yes, I agree.
Well, that seems to be clear then.
If the coffee Shop doesn’t improve, we won’t be renewing Oliver Rogers contract.
Can you inform Oliver Rogers about our feelings, Donnie?
Yes. We can send him an email today.
OK, good. Let’s see how it goes then.
OK, let's move on to the next item on the agenda.
The Eat Yourself Fitter Week.
How’s the preparation coming along?
Right well. Myself and Pat attended the Eat Yourself Fitter Week Organising Committee meeting last week and dates have now been fixed Hold on I’ve just got them here Yeah,
it’s running from March the 5th to March 10th Really?
So Yeah. Well, the committee also discussed the events and things that’ll happen through the week.
The first thing was the issue of setting up stalls on campus and I was given the task of coming up with some ideas.
What I thought of was to set up some stalls on campus What different kinds of food.
Sounds good. But what do you mean?
Cooked food or?
Yeah, Yeah, cooked food but that’s cooked healthily.
Right. And the name we’ve come up with is Healthy Hawker Stalls I like it.
Healthy Hawker Stalls It’s quite catchy.
Yes, Well, the next thing discussed was to hold a lecture, especially for the Eat Yourself Fitter Week.
OK. We asked Antonio Zacha if she would like to give the lecture.
Who? You know Antonio Zacha, the owner of the new restaurant on campus.
No. You’ve lost me.
Antonio, Zacha. Z -A -C -H -A.
She’s opening the new restaurant at the university.
Oh, Sorry, I know.
Antonio Zacha. The Chef.
Right. So is she going to do a lecture, then?
Yes. She was actually really keen.
She’s actually keen to help in any way she can in the Eat Yourself Fitter Week.
Well, let’s try to get her involved.
When’s her lecture on again?
OK, we’ve booked the room already.
Just let me find it Oh, OK, yeah, Thursday March the 8th At 1 p .m.
And she’ll be talking in Lecture Room 14b.
Now, The title of her lecture is Eating on a Budget Right, let me make a quick note of that.
Antonio Zaca Eating on a Budget.
Thursday the 8th at 1 o 'clock.
Oh, and we’ve got a slogan.
what? You know, a slogan.
A sentence to put on the poster.
For the Eat Yourself fit a Week.
Oh, OK. A slogan.
We thought of it the other day to encourage students to eat better.
how did it go again.
Oh yeah, it was Down with Salt, Sugar and Fat I like it.
What was it again.
Down with Salt, Sugar and Fat Yeah.
Good. Great. Right, we’ll get that on the banner as well.
OK, well you’ve certainly been busy there.
Maybe you can give us a further update on progress in the next meeting.
